thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH LATENCY ALERT for dedicated-pool-prod-3 — p95 > 500ms, p99 > 2s for last 3m. Queues growing. Paging kevin-oncall and oncall rotation.

kevin-oncall: acked. I'm seeing the paging. Pulling traces now.

kevin-oncall: summary from dashboards: sustained queue depth ~110 on pool prod-3, active replicas 6, target was 8 but autoscaler hasn't finished warmup for 2 nodes. p99 is dominated by streaming stalls (clients waiting on first chunk).

jonathan-eng-runtime: I can confirm. Metrics from runtime: warmup latency for new nodes spiked to 45s due to container image pull + model mmap; scaling decision executed ~80s ago but node not Ready until ~2m. Autoscaler logs show "warmup_timeout_retry" entries.

maria-ops: any recent infra changes? kube cluster scaling policy tweaked yesterday?

dmitri-sre: infra team rolled the node image to include kernel 5.15 patch at 03:00 UTC. That changed container runtime pulls from mirror A -> B fallback. Could explain image pull slowness.

jonathan-eng-runtime: also seeing KV cache priming causing CPU pressure during warmup; when new replica comes up it pulls model shards then blocks the warmup endpoint for older requests. Head-of-line blocking.

sasha-support: we have two customer-reported cases (Cust A, Cust F) noting slow responses and partial streaming. Support has acknowledged and posted updates.

kevin-oncall: immediate mitigations I propose: 1) enable manual scale-up of prod-3 to +2 warm replicas (if available in reserved pool) 2) apply temporary rate-limit/routing to move heavy customers to hosted fallback model where possible 3) enable graceful-serve mode to favor small requests to reduce tail. Any objections?

jonathan-eng-runtime: +1 to manual scale. I'm worried adding replicas will take ~90s before they help. For routing fallback, we can flip a route to fallback-model-1 (lower capacity but cold start is warm) — need Ops help to avoid data plane outage.

maria-ops: starting manual scale now. Command: `infractl pool scale prod-3 --replicas 8 --reason "incident 1901122334"`

incident-bot: Runbook step executed by maria-ops: manual-scale invoked.

dmitri-sre: checking autoscaler history: 2026-03-14T03:12:01Z decision to scale +2, but warmup_policy=sequential so it waits for jitted kernels. We have a bug where warmup_policy sequential delays multiple nodes; open PR to change to parallel-warmup next week. Not helpful now.

jonathan-eng-runtime: We can temporarily set `RUNTIME_WARMUP_PARALLEL=true` for prod-3 but that requires a config rollout. Could do a safe runtime config flip via console with zero-downtime.

kevin-oncall: do it. maria, please coordinate the config flip; jonathan, be ready to rollback.

maria-ops: flipping Runtime config: `redwoodctl config set prod-3 RUNTIME_WARMUP_PARALLEL true --apply`

incident-bot: Config change submitted by maria-ops, rollout started.

jonathan-eng-runtime: rollout in progress. Watching kernel/jit logs. Note: parallel warmup increases disk IO and network egress transiently. Keep an eye on node-level thrashing.

kevin-oncall: meanwhile, Sasha — post an interim customer update: we are investigating latency spikes, mitigation in progress. Use this wording: "We detected increased tail latency for dedicated pools affecting some requests. We're scaling capacity and routing heavy workloads to fallbacks. We'll update in 30 minutes."

sasha-support: Posted. Ticket threads updated for Cust A and Cust F.

maria-ops: manual scale returned success: replicas now 8. New nodes started; initial readiness coming in at +70s.

jonathan-eng-runtime: I see new replicas Ready. However streaming stalls persist for some in-flight sessions — likely stale connections pinned to the previously overloaded workers. We should gracefully drain old workers.

dmitri-sre: draining old pods now: `kubectl cordon & drain` with maxUnavailable=1.

kevin-oncall: also enabling short-term request-shed for long-running streaming connections >45s (config `STREAM_MAX_ACTIVE_MS=45000`). This will free queue headroom.

jonathan-eng-runtime: applied stream cap. Telemetry shows p95 dropping to ~220ms, p99 trending down from 2.1s -> 900ms over next 2m.

incident-bot: DETECTED: p95 back to SLO threshold, p99 improving. Continue monitoring for 15m.

sasha-support: customers acknowledged update: Cust A reports improved latency. :thumbsup:

maria-ops: follow-up actions: 1) incident cause = autoscaler warmup sequential policy + image pull latency due to mirror fallback. 2) mitigation = manual scale + parallel warmup toggle + draining old pods + temporary stream cap + routing fallback for heavy clients. 3) postmortem owner: jonathan-eng-runtime.

jonathan-eng-runtime: taking postmortem. I'll gather traces, autoscaler logs, and warmup timing buckets. ETA for draft: EOD today.

dmitri-sre: I'll open infra ticket to verify image mirror performance and add a health-check for image pull times. Also propose autoscaler tweak: if queue depth > 80 and pending_warm_nodes > 0, allow parallel warmup immediately.

kevin-oncall: Handoff: I'm going offline in 30m. Handoff to dmitri-sre for overnight watch. Key watch items: queue depth, p99, any container image pull spikes. If p99 > 1.5s for >5m, escalate to ENG runtime pager.

dmitri-sre: ack. I'll take over. Kept in the loop: jonathan-eng-runtime, maria-ops, sasha-support.

sasha-support: I'll send a customer follow-up after the postmortem is ready.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Created ticket IN-1901122334 with summary "Dedicated pool warmup delay caused p99 SLO breach; manual mitigations applied."

kevin-oncall: closing my watch. Thanks everyone.

dmitri-sre: leaving a note in the ticket: root cause hypothesis + action items (infra mirror, autoscaler parallel warmup, runtime warmup optimizations, doc update for oncall runbook).

jonathan-eng-runtime: added perf graphs and logs to the ticket. Will attach flamegraphs for a sample stalled streaming session.

sasha-support: marking customer updates and will follow up when postmortem published.

maria-ops: final check: system metrics stable for 10m. Good to hand to postmortem.

incident-bot: Thread closed for new alerts. Monitor channel for follow-ups.
